messages.subject: SelectInput, Reactivity, jQuery
parts:
Hi, I am a total newbie when it comes to programming.
I am trying to make an application where it does following:
1. scrape web data - DONE
2. show data on Shiny - DONE

So both are done, then why am I posting here?

I have a little problem understanding reactivity with my renderDataTable's dependencies.
==========
ui.R
library(shiny)
library(shinyIncubator)
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  includeHTML("helper.js"),
  
  fluidRow(
    column(3,
           textInput("businessName", label="Query"),
           textInput("businessLocation", label="Location"),
           actionButton("searchAction", "Search")
           ),
    column(3,
           h4("Search Result"),
           selectInput("search_result",
                       "",
                       "Please search first",
                       selected=NULL,
                       selectize=FALSE)
           ),
    column(4,
           h4("Business Info"),
           uiOutput("business_info")
           ),
    column(2,
           uiOutput("business_image")
           )
  ),
  hr(),
  progressInit(),
  dataTableOutput("table")
))

==========
server.R
library(shiny)
library(shinyIncubator)
source("test.R")
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  
  business_list <- reactive({
    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    withProgress(session, min=0, max=10, {
      setProgress(message="Searching",
                  detail="This may take a while...")
      isolate({
        result <- search_business(input$businessName, input$businessLocation)
      })
      for (i in 1:50) {
        setProgress(value = i)
      }
      return(result)
    })
    
  })
  
  get_business_data <- reactive({
    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    if (is.null(input$selIdx)) return()
    if (input$selIdx == 0) return()
    withProgress(session, min=0, max=10, {
      setProgress(message="Downloading reviews",
                  detail="This may take a while...")
      data <- get_data(business_list()$id[input$selIdx])
      for (i in 1:50) {
        setProgress(value = i)
      }
      return(data)
    })
  })
  
  observe({
    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    updateSelectInput(session,
                      "search_result",
                      "",
                      c(if(business_list()$name[1] != "No result") "Please select a restaurant",
                        as.character(business_list()$name)),
                      selected=NULL)
  })
  
  output$table <- renderDataTable({
   if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
   if (is.null(input$selIdx)) return()
   data <- get_business_data()
   data
 },option=list(iDisplayLength=10,
               bAutoWidth=FALSE,
               aoColumns=NULL,
               aoColumnDefs = list(list(sWidth="7em",
                                        aTargets=c(list(0),list(1))))))
  
  output$business_info <- renderUI({
    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    if (is.null(input$selIdx)) return()
    if (input$selIdx == 0) return()
    name <- paste("<b>Name: </b>", as.character(business_list()$name[input$selIdx]), sep="")
    rating <- paste("<b>Rating: </b>", as.character(business_list()$rating[input$selIdx]), sep="")
    address <- paste("<b>Address: </b>", as.character(business_list()$address[input$selIdx]), sep="")
    url <- paste("<b>URL: </b>", as.character(business_list()$url_b[input$selIdx]), sep="")
    HTML(paste(name, rating, address, url, sep="<br/>"))
  })
  
  output$business_image <- renderUI({
    if (input$searchAction == 0) return()
    if (is.null(input$selIdx)) return()
    if (input$selIdx == 0) return()
    image_b <- paste("<br/><img src='",
                     as.character(business_list()$image_b[input$selIdx]),
                     "' alt='business-image' height='150' width='150'>",
                     sep="")
    HTML(image_b)
  })

  
})


When I run this, the whole application works flawlessly up to a point.
The workflow is like this:
1. Get inputs from users for input$businessName & input$businessLocation
2. If the user clicks the "Search" action button, then call API (search API) to retrieve data
3. With that list, updateSelectInput
4. If index of SelectInput changes, then !!update!! business_info & business_image & table

To check for the index of SelectInput I use this jQuery syntax

<script type="text/javascript">

$(document).ready(function(){
$(document).on('change', '#search_result', function() {
Shiny.onInputChange('selIdx', this.selectedIndex);
});
})

</script>

Step 1-4 works fine, unless I click the "Search" action button.
When I search for a different query, and click the action button, then $(document).on('change', '#search_result', function() this is fired again, running step 4 even though it should not (because I set selected=NULL).

I think I have a really poor understanding of reactivity using jQuery since I learned R and Shiny about 2 weeks ago.
Could anyone help me out?
Shiny is so nice in terms of how reactivity is there with dataset and for web applications, and I wish to learn it more extensively!

Thanks in advance.
